item.title: ShotgunDAgger: An Imitation Learning Algorithm for End‐to‐End Autonomous Driving Without Intervention Based on HD Map
item.description: Transactions in GIS, Volume 30, Issue 6, September 2026.
item.dc:description: ABSTRACTDataset Aggregation (DAgger) mitigates covariate shift in imitation learning by aggregating expert‐labeled data from learner‐influenced rollouts, but intervention‐based implementations can require costly real‐time supervision in autonomous driving. We propose ShotgunDAgger, an HD‐map‐assisted framework in which learner actions remain in control while a rule‐based navigation stack supplies supervision. ShotgunDAgger1 replans the expert reference trajectory when the HD‐map gate detects lane‐ or route‐level deviation; ShotgunDAgger2 truncates the rollout and resets the simulator to avoid collecting severely deviated states. Experiments in CARLA compare the two variants with BC, DAgger, and HG‐DAgger under noiseless and action‐noise conditions. ShotgunDAgger2 achieves favorable collision, episode‐length, and driving‐distance results among the learned policies, particularly under moderate and strong action noise. The current gate uses lane‐segment identifiers and planned‐route waypoints, providing a practical foundation for incorporating richer HD‐map semantics into imitation learning data collection.
item.content:encoded:
ABSTRACT

Dataset Aggregation (DAgger) mitigates covariate shift in imitation learning by aggregating expert-labeled data from learner-influenced rollouts, but intervention-based implementations can require costly real-time supervision in autonomous driving. We propose ShotgunDAgger, an HD-map-assisted framework in which learner actions remain in control while a rule-based navigation stack supplies supervision. ShotgunDAgger1 replans the expert reference trajectory when the HD-map gate detects lane- or route-level deviation; ShotgunDAgger2 truncates the rollout and resets the simulator to avoid collecting severely deviated states. Experiments in CARLA compare the two variants with BC, DAgger, and HG-DAgger under noiseless and action-noise conditions. ShotgunDAgger2 achieves favorable collision, episode-length, and driving-distance results among the learned policies, particularly under moderate and strong action noise. The current gate uses lane-segment identifiers and planned-route waypoints, providing a practical foundation for incorporating richer HD-map semantics into imitation learning data collection.
